verdicts.evidence: Numerical experiments on K-bin discrete policies show the objective is non-linear (chord gap [1.037e-4, 8.139e-2] vs 2.22e-16 for linear baseline), multi-criterion adaptation outperforms naive in 60/60 cases, and the N=1 mutation collapses non-linearity to 3.33e-16 with identical optima.

Functional derivative matches finite differences to max abs error 8.285e-10 over 80 cases; drop-in replacement on standard GRPO reaches true optimum (max suboptimality 5.55e-16); empirical π̂ approximation shows O(1/M) convergence (log-log slope −1.024); plain-reward mutation is strictly worse in 30/30 instances.

Across 90 instances and 2250 bound evaluations with numerically estimated L, zero violations above 1e-12 (44 raw ratio>1 rows are all double-precision noise at LHS ≤3.33e-16); step-size mutation (η=20/L) yields 11 macroscopic violations and plain-reward mutation yields 36/36 violations.

Over 60 configs × 200 runs, the full bound with 2(ε+δ)/β is never violated (max ratio 0.2611); dropping the bias term violates 36/36 noisy configs (max ratio 1.65e10); plateau grows monotonically with noise in 12/12 cells.

Sympy confirms the density normalizes; first-order optimality at claimed π* holds to machine precision (span ≤5.84e-16 for N=2–16); naive optimum puts mass 1.0 at y≈0.5 (δ_0.5 collapse) vs 0.922 bimodal mass for IAMA N=8; exponent mutation (1/N vs 1/(N−1)) breaks optimality by 14 orders of magnitude.

No experiments were run; the logbook reports blocking constraints including GPU-cluster scale for 7B RL training, unreleased author-trained reward models, no public code, and no numeric table behind Fig. 6b.

overall: The logbook provides thorough numerical verification of the paper's five theoretical claims through discrete-distribution experiments with mutation tests, cross-checks against independent solvers, and finite-difference validation. The empirical LLM claim (Claim 6) is honestly reported as unreproduced due to GPU scale, unreleased models, and missing code.
